bounded_sandbox_diagnostic.decision_basis: Both independently frozen sources time out without an initialization marker, then pass the same exact read-denial assertions after one identical explicit prewarm. The original full-suite timeouts each bind to seven filesystem helper cold-start attempts within that exact test interval. Relevant test/dispatch/setup/fs-helper files are byte-identical.

invalidated_diagnostic_artifacts.reason: Shared target reused the control binary: 3642 rather than 3675 tests; the purported current 180-second run is a control repetition.
The same pre-cleanup control binary was reused; the current label is invalid.

diagnostic_history.conclusion: The initial checkout/application sequence allowed global autocrlf to rewrite 62 changed files. Raw tree 743778b39e5dbb7a5ee171040ceb1f51dc4e4d99 was diagnostic only. Every difference from the canonical 45f946 tree was CRLF versus LF. The corrected source was rebuilt; diagnostic candidate 223195f76b7c527d97003a555174b51552258627d09ef3355a9abc749e4a25af was not qualified.

887 tests: 878 passed, one concurrent parent-claim failure, four macOS fixture errors, four skips. The harness also changed during this run, so it is diagnostic. The failed concurrent fixture was preserved. The original Git-status stderr was not captured and its exact cause remains unknown.
100 targeted iterations and the shared-index-reader control did not reproduce the initial intermittent Git-status failure. These green runs do not explain that failure.

A separate deterministic test proved snapshot collection refreshed the Git index. Disabling optional locks alone still failed; also disabling diff.autoRefreshIndex produced two passing tests. This correction is proven for snapshot index mutation, not established as the root cause of the original intermittent status failure.

The first clean rerun had 892=884 passed+8 host skips but only 84/85 equivalences because a temporary-root test was renamed. An explicit old-to-current test ID mapping and a fail-closed audit test restored 85/85; the next run was 893=885 passed+8 skips. The final frozen f5 run is 908=900 passed+8 host skips, 85/85.

The earlier c5 native positive wrote the exact owned file using relative qualified.txt and exited successfully, but its owner checker accepted only an absolute patch header. That run remains an unconsumed harness-negative and is not qualification evidence. The f5 checker accepts only the exact basename or canonical absolute form for the same single operation/body and owned path. Traversal, drive-relative, foreign, and multi-operation forms remain rejected; new f5 live evidence was collected.

The first targeted command supplied duplicate nextest thread options and ran no tests. The unmodified release integration constructor aborted because test-binary-support uses a temporary HOME while codex-arg0 rejects temp helper aliases without debug assertions. Both files match exact upstream. A symmetric test-only codex-arg0 debug-assertions override was approved; the production CLI was unchanged. Initial collectors looked under CARGO_TARGET_DIR instead of source/target/nextest/local; their zero-case records remain, with exact PASS/Summary and the preserved protocol JUnit harvested separately.

Clean upstream --locked failed before compilation/tests because Cargo.lock retained 149 workspace package versions at 0.0.0 while the release workspace version was 0.153.4. An isolated base + exact Cargo.lock workspace-version delta control was used. All 149 changed packages have no source; registry/git dependencies, checksums, dependency lists and all other fields are identical. The original upstream checkout and candidate source were preserved. This is not a claim that the clean base passed --locked.

Two older failures (missing child capsule/binding and missing durable parent conflict) lost their original fixtures. Later controlled schedules cannot retroactively explain them. They remain recorded in the predecessor audit history.
